rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while limiting the time penalty. The elution window will guide subsequent narrowing and slope or temperature tests.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while testing the critical pair’s response to slope.

Both methods already attain the maximum CRF, but the shorter gradient leaves the critical pair near its resolution threshold. Raise temperature at fixed slope to test whether selectivity permits a faster fully resolved run.

The temperature increase improved the critical middle pair while preserving full resolution. Shorten the gradient one step to test the speed limit, retaining injection 3 as the fastest fully resolved method so far.

The six-minute gradient was too steep for the critical middle pair. Lowering phi1 to 0.80 gives an intermediate slope that should recover resolution while remaining faster than injection 3 and keeping the last peak within the gradient.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving the slope that achieved full resolution in injection 5. This should reduce retention times; the main check is whether the early and critical middle pairs retain sufficient resolution.

Raise the starting organic fraction to shorten retention while slightly flattening the gradient to protect the middle pair, which is close to the resolution threshold. Monitor the early pair for compression as initial retention decreases.

Continue raising phi0 by one step to shorten the fully resolved run. The accompanying shallower slope may protect the middle pair, while the early pair will reveal whether the starting organic fraction is becoming too high.

Test one further increase in starting organic fraction for a faster maximum-score method. Both the early pair and middle pair now have limited margin, so this run will help locate the upper useful phi0 boundary.

The maximum CRF is already secured, so test a much faster alternative for a possible selectivity crossover of the critical middle pair. Return to 40 C to give the early pair more separation; this exploratory run may sacrifice resolution.

Explore the fast-gradient regime at lower temperature and a higher starting organic fraction to seek separation beyond the middle-pair crossover. Lower temperature should help retain the early compounds despite the higher phi0; injection 8 remains the fastest verified maximum-score method.

Return to the promising region near injection 9 and flatten its gradient slightly to recover the middle pair’s resolution. This may achieve full resolution with a last peak earlier than injection 8’s 3.45 minutes.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 12 to lift the middle pair above R = 1.5, while trimming the unused upper gradient window. The last peak should remain inside the gradient, with retention near the fastest fully resolved run.

Test whether a further temperature increase improves middle-pair selectivity enough to support a faster gradient. Lower phi0 than injection 13 to protect early retention, and check the first pair carefully for temperature-driven convergence.

Return to 50 C to restore early-pair selectivity and use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 8 to strengthen the middle pair. This targets a short maximum-score method with more resolution margin than the fastest verified conditions.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at lower temperature, which should help retain the early compounds while changing middle-pair selectivity. This explores another route to a faster fully resolved method; injection 13 remains the fastest verified maximum-score run.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a trimmed gradient with more resolution margin than the fastest method. Relative to injection 15, lowering the window at unchanged slope should improve initial retention while keeping all peaks well within ten minutes.

Test a two-minute gradient with a shallower slope to protect the critical middle pair, followed by a hold. The lower endpoint may delay the last peak, but this checks whether a compact gradient can retain maximum CRF without approaching the ten-minute penalty threshold.

Test a slope just steeper than injection 8, returning to 50 C to restore the early-pair resolution lost in injection 14. This targets a last peak near 3.4 minutes, with the middle pair determining whether full resolution survives.

Test temperature robustness around injection 15’s fully resolved, compact gradient. A five-degree reduction should improve early-pair separation; the middle pair will determine whether maximum CRF is maintained.

Check a five-degree temperature reduction around injection 13, the fastest verified maximum-score method. This isolates temperature sensitivity at its higher starting organic fraction and tests whether the critical middle pair remains fully resolved.

Flatten the gradient one step relative to injection 13 to increase the critical middle pair’s resolution margin. This should preserve maximum CRF with only a modest retention increase and keep the last peak within the gradient.

Test whether injection 22’s shallower gradient preserves full resolution at 45 C, where the early pair separates better. The added middle-pair margin may yield a less temperature-sensitive maximum-score method.
Test a slope between injections 13 and 22 to balance speed and resolution margin near the fastest fully resolved method. This should retain maximum CRF with less delay than injection 22.

Test injection 24’s intermediate slope at 45 C; nearby results suggest the middle pair should remain fully resolved while early-pair separation improves. This final refinement targets another maximum-score method, with injection 13 retained as the fastest verified fully resolved option.
